findings.source_quote: πῶς ὑμεῖς παιδεύειν θέλετε τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς Κυρίου, αὐτοὶ μὴ ἔχοντες παιδείαν;
findings.english_quote: How can you want to teach the Lord’s chosen ones when you yourselves have not been taught?
findings.issue: The source describes the leaders as presently lacking training or discipline. “Have not been taught” instead asserts a history of not receiving teaching. Those are not equivalent: people can have received teaching while still lacking the training or discipline criticized here.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “How can you want to train the Lord’s chosen ones when you yourselves lack training?” Review the replacement afresh for the contextual sense of παιδεία and its relationship to the repeated παιδεύω verbs.

findings.source_quote: παιδεύετε οὖν ἀλλήλους καὶ εἰρηνεύετε ἐν αὐτοῖς, ἵνα κἀγὼ κατέναντι τοῦ πατρὸς ἱλαρὰ σταθεῖσα λόγον ἀποδῶ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν πάντων τῷ Κυρίῳ ὑμῶν.
findings.english_quote: Teach one another and be at peace among them. Then I too may stand joyfully before the Father and give an account for all of you to your Lord[g].
findings.issue: The source explicitly connects the commands with the speaker’s accounting through ἵνα. The separate sentence beginning “Then” makes temporal succession explicit but leaves the source’s purpose relationship implicit. This loses a stated grammatical relationship rather than merely simplifying sentence length.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “Train one another and be at peace among them, so that I too, standing joyfully before the Father, may give an account for all of you to your Lord.” Review this proposal afresh; retain the disclosed ambiguity of “among them.”

findings.english_quote: Preserve all ten paragraphs, warnings and purposes, source brackets, different speakers and the three appearances.
findings.issue: The simplification metadata incorrectly describes this selected section as containing different speakers and three appearances. IX contains one continuous address; it does not narrate three appearances. This is a concrete scope error in the supplied editorial account, even though the English body does not introduce those events.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove the claims about different speakers and three appearances. Describe this section’s ten paragraphs, warnings, purpose clauses, editorial brackets, and continuous first-person address instead. Any claim about another section requires its own source and review.

summary: The standard edition faithfully covers the selected working Greek, including its difficult readings, negations, warnings, and editorial bracket, without substituting disclosed variants. Its witness notes are compatible with the supplied bounded project reports; this does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify an exhaustive collation. The simplified edition requires correction of the present lack of training, explicit final purpose relationship, and inaccurate scope metadata. Neither edition introduces a servant- or repentance-terminology conflict in this section. Proposed replacements remain subject to fresh review.
